name: Kanikkaran
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Only Bhattacharya 1976 comparative note and a Language-in-India sociolinguistic article (read; no stress mention).

sources.citation: Agesthialingom, S. 1976. Kanikkara Dialect. (Dialect Studies 5.) Annamalainagar: Annamalai University. xii+155 pp. [Kanikkar Tamil of Kanyakumari district, Tamil Nadu]
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online: WID Offsite Storage PL4759.A35 (also: hathitrust digitized, search-only (in copyright))
sources.note: Nothing on stress placement. Sec. 1.3 'Suprasegmental Phonemes' (p. 8) treats only vowel length as a suprasegmental phoneme; footnote 1 on the same page: 'other suprasegmental features occurring in this dialect have not been taken for analysis in this study.' Allophones (1.5), clusters (1.6) and syllabic patterns (1.7, pp. 26-28) contain no stress/accent statement.

sources.citation: Shyam, S. K.; Pugazhendi, P.; Mini, P. V. 2019. 'Chetham' (Sabdam): Kani bhasha sahayi - Preparation of a Handbook for Kani Language of Kanikkar Community in Kerala State. Kozhikode: KIRTADS. 296 pp. (in Malayalam) [Kerala Kani]
sources.note: Silent. Ch. II phonology (pp. 44 ff.) gives 5 short + 5 long vowels, diphthongs, 24 consonants, positional distribution, identical and non-identical clusters, then goes straight to nouns; no section or remark on uunnal/stress, syllable or prosody (Malayalam scanned searched for ഊന്നല്‍, ബലാഘാതം, അക്ഷരഘടന and English 'stress/accent').

sources.citation: Soni, M. K. 2014. Thiruvananthapuram-Kollam jillakalile Kanikkarude ulsavangalum vamozhi vazhakkavum: oru padanam. PhD thesis, Dept. of Malayalam, University of Kerala. 443 pp. (in Malayalam); ch. 5 'Kanikkarude vamozhivazhakkam', subsection 'Kanibhasha' pp. 326-328.
sources.note: Silent. Folklore thesis; the language subsection has only sociolinguistic remarks (Tamil-Malayalam mixed speech, south vs north of Neyyattinkara distinguishable by pronunciation) and sample dialogues; scanned with tesseract mal+eng at 150 dpi because the PDF text layer is custom-font garbage.

sources.citation: Nair, Ravi Sankar S. 2013. Tribal Languages of Kerala. Language in India 13(7): 1-58 (ch. 7 'Kani', pp. 31-32).
sources.note: Silent. Kani section lists segmental correspondences with Malayalam (a>e, v>m/b, rr>cc, l>y) and a few morphological features; no mention of stress or accent.

sources.citation: van der Hulst, Harry & Rob Goedemans (eds.) 2010. A survey of word accentual patterns in the languages of the world, Asia chapter (StressTyp) - local text copy under synchro/tropics/
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: online with a university library login (also: harvard online access (harvardkey); publisher (doi, likely paywalled))
sources.note: Kanikkaran appears only in the Dravidian classification list ('UNCLASSIFIED: Allar, Bazigar, Bharia, Kamar, Kanikkaran,...'); no accent data for it.
